key_insight: The study shows that reinforcement learning can improve a language model’s clinical reasoning for colon cancer treatment planning even when the “right” answer is only partially verifiable.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help decision-support systems learn more realistic, stepwise oncology planning by rewarding good information gathering and defensible treatment choices, not just final answers.
method: Formulated colon cancer treatment planning as a partially observable interactive RL task.
Built patient-specific, process-aware rewards from real-world clinical records.
Optimized Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with GRPO and GDPO to sequentially collect information before recommending first-line treatment.
evidence_signal: In the reported interactive environment, the GDPO-trained policy improved Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by 79.60% over the base Llama model and outperformed GPT-5.2 by 18.82%, while also reducing training query count.
watch_item: Because the environment and rewards are derived from retrospective records, performance may not fully translate to prospective clinical use without careful validation.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
